messages:
maria: heads up — eu-west3 swarm: sudden NVMe scrub ramp on scratchpool after this morning's kernel rollout (5.15 -> 6.2). GPU provisioning is stalled, ~28 pending GPU allocs stuck in attach phase. iops on /dev/nvme0n1 at 300k/s on some hosts. paging logs attached below.

jake: ugh, any node ids?

maria: gnode-1103, gnode-1107, gnode-1112, gnode-1120, gnode-1135 — scrubber process eating IO and causing eviction spikes.

priyanka: noted. this looks like the janitor scrub scheduler not honouring the new kernel's block layer changes. can we throttle scrub concurrency per-node until we get a proper fix?

maria: yeah i was thinking throttle + prefer-cold-gpu-routing to avoid blocking critical jobs.

opsbot: ALERT: eu-west3 nvme-scrub-iops spike detected — 28 hosts throttled by autoscaler at 2024-10-02T08:12:11Z.

lee: quick mitigations: 1) reduce janitor concurrency, 2) temporarily disable full-scrub cron for scratchpool, 3) route new GPU requests to eu-west1/eu-west4. which one do we want now?

jake: can we do (1) + (3) asap. disabling scrubs entirely worries me for wear/corruption.

priyanka: agreed. small config change: set `janitor.scrub_concurrency=2` and drop `scrub_backoff_ms` to 2000 for rollout. example:

```yaml
# /etc/redwood/janitor.yaml
pool: scratchpool
scan: full
scrub_concurrency: 2
scrub_backoff_ms: 2000
```

priyanka: then `systemctl restart redwood-janitor` will pick it up. i'll push via orchestration in the next 2 mins.

maria: doing gradual roll: start on the 28 affected hosts, then fanout. please watch GPU attach queue.

deploy-bot: deploy job 9321 queued: apply janitor config change to eu-west3 (28 hosts).

jake: if anyone needs the quick node-level throttle, you can echo into the debug endpoint: `curl -XPOST http://gnode-1103:8080/debug/janitor?concurrency=1` — only for emergency manual ops.

lee: question — do we have disk SMART errors or actual badblocks? could be later-stage wear triggered by kernel driver's scheduling.

maria: so far SMART is fine; dmesg shows repeated `nvme core: scrub read timeout` and `blk_mq_dispatch` latencies. no crc errors yet. logs: 

```
Oct 02 08:08:02 gnode-1103 kernel: nvme0n1: async scrub start seq=4123
Oct 02 08:08:07 gnode-1103 kernel: blk_mq: issue timeout for tag 436, bdev nvme0n1
Oct 02 08:08:07 gnode-1103 kernel: nvme0n1: read timeout, retrying (cnt=1)
Oct 02 08:09:14 gnode-1103 systemd[1]: redwood-janitor.service: schedule-run
```
priyanka: thanks. i'll gate the change behind a feature-flag so we can revert quickly. also i'll update the reduce-concurrency playbook to include a `--gpu-routing=avoid-eu-west3` hint.

maria: routing change = set `region_avoid: eu-west3` on the provisioner for 30m, then let autoscaler rebalance. who wants to own that?

jake: i'll take routing. i'll put a temporary placement rule on the provisioner and watch costs.

lee: long term we need a kernel-aware scrub scheduler upstream or revert kernel in the staging lane. ops/infra meeting to decide later.

priyanka: FYI cost note — temporary region routing will increase egress and instance costs by ~12% for impacted jobs; i'll notify finance slack.

maria: results after throttling: within 5 mins iops dropped to ~40k/s on the worst hosts, gpu attach queue drained from 28 -> 3.

opsbot: INFO: janitor config rollout completed on 28 hosts at 2024-10-02T08:19:42Z.

jake: nice. leaving routing in place for 30 minutes. can we monitor for correlation with wear counters?

priyanka: added a short-term telemetry job to sample nvme SMART attributes every 2 mins for the affected nodes. output will feed into the grafana panel `infra.nvme.scrub` for the triage channel.

maria: follow-up actions: (A) open kernel bug with vendor + attach logs (i'll do), (B) pick one of: upstream scrub scheduler fix or kernel rollback for stable pool, (C) document temporary throttle play in runbook.

lee: i've scheduled a quick postmortem sync in 30m to decide rollback vs patch. ping me if regressions reappear. :eyes: 

jake: thanks all — thumbs up if you're good with the plan. :thumbsup: 

priyanka: :thumbsup: will write runbook snippet and notify support.

maria: closing the incident channel when postmortem scheduled. thanks everyone.
